##段落
让我们别再称它们为“软技能”——改叫“真技能”吧  
2023年6月9日  
/  
赛斯·戈丁  
Facebook  
X  
LinkedIn  
Reddit  
WhatsApp  
黛博拉·斯皮尔曼  
我们仍然像经营保龄球队一样招聘和培训，仿佛只有那些容易衡量的技能才重要。

##段落
是什么导致成功组织走向失败？是什么让股票下跌、创新放缓、客户流失？我们都能认同某些技能是必不可少的。招聘不会写代码的程序员、不会销售的销售员或不会设计的建筑师，纯属浪费。但这些技能——让我们称它们为“职业技能”——已成为招聘流程的支柱。

##段落
但你怎么解释，拥有同样职业技能的相似组织，却往往结果迥异？学生们接触的大多数教科书和参加的考试，都聚焦于职业技能，即那些为了获得工作而必须勾选的条条框框。通过错误定义“职业”并专注于这些所谓的关键技能，我们贬低了其他重要技能的价值。

##段落
当我们称其他技能为“软”技能，暗示它们是可有可无的，我们就对它们尊重不足。真正区分繁荣组织与挣扎组织的，是那些难以衡量的态度、流程和从业者的认知。

##段落
职业技能可以被传授：你并非天生就懂工程、文案或平面设计，因此它们必定是可以教的东西。但在决策、积极参与、与恐惧共舞、有权威地表达、团队合作、看清真相、说出真相、激励他人、超越要求地付出、关心他人以及愿意改变这些事情上，我们却让自己逃脱了责任。我们在这方面的培训投入不足，担心这些东西是天生的、无法传授的。或许它们是天赋。于是我们轻描淡写，称它们为软技能，让我们轻易转向看似更紧迫的事情。

##段落
在规模层面，组织在招聘时对软技能的关注较少，因为我们说服自己职业技能是非个人的、更容易衡量。如果更容易测试，它似乎在选团队时就更重要。

##段落
而当这些技能缺失时，我们解雇缓慢（且很少再培训），因为我们担心踩到别人的脚趾、被指责过于个人化，或可能在无望的事情上浪费时间。

##段落
但这些技能全都可以学会，就像下棋或打字这类显而易见的技能可以学会一样。我们是通过偶然、耳濡目染、通过与老师、父母、老板和世界的碰撞而学会它们的。即使它们更难衡量，那也不意味着我们无法改进、无法练习。

我们无法改变工作方式吗？  
当然可以。  
别再称它们为“软技能”了。它们是人际技能，是领导技能，是魅力、勤奋和贡献的技能。但这些修饰词虽然准确，却不知何故将它们与职业技能、我们实际招聘时看重的技能、我们衡量研究生学位的技能拉开了距离。  
所以，让我们不自在地称它们为“真实技能”。  
真实，因为它们有效，因为它们是我们今天所需的核心。  
真实，因为即使你拥有职业技能，没有这些人类技能——那些我们无法写下来或编程让计算机去做的事情——你对我们毫无帮助。  
真实技能当然不能取代职业技能。它们能做的是放大你已经在衡量的东西。  
想象一个拥有所有传统职业技能的团队成员：高效、熟练、经验丰富，简历可以证明这一切。那是一个不错的基线。  
现在再加上：敏锐、有魅力、有驱动力、专注、目标明确、鼓舞人心且积极主动。慷慨、富有同理心且始终如一。耐心倾听，深入理解。当这样一个人加入你的团队时，你的组织会发生什么变化？  
在《哈佛商业评论》中，卢·所罗门报道，69%的管理者与员工沟通时感到不适。我猜其他31%中许多人是在撒谎。  
与员工沟通之所以不适，是因为我们建立了顺从和支配的系统，使沟通变得困难。我们要求人们把人性留在门外，然后用权威来改变行为。我们将企业贪婪和短期思维与创造有意义工作的渴望叠加在一起。  
我们如何建立以人为本的组织，同时接受这样一个事实：我们三分之二的管理者（想必薪酬优厚、训练有素且对我们的成功至关重要）在做一项基本工作时如此不适，以至于向陌生人承认了这一点？  
在最近的一项调查中，研究生入学管理委员会报告称，尽管MBA在分析能力、量化专长和信息收集能力方面很强，但他们在雇主同样看重的其他关键领域严重欠缺：战略思维、书面和口头沟通、领导力和适应性。这些是相互排斥的吗？我们必须牺牲一个来换取另一个吗？  
所有真实技能的基础是这一点：拥有彼此交谈的自信和许可。不是去管理、贬低、恐吓或控制。只是寻求被理解，并努力去理解。  
摘自赛斯·高汀的《意义之歌：团队新宣言》，经企鹅兰登书屋旗下投资组合出版社同意转载。

readings.title: How social media ceased to be social
body: 22 May 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google John Laurenson Social media platforms used to be about communication between friends – now many are increasingly short video entertainment hubs. The business model is to increase the time people spend on their apps and increase ad revenue. But is there already a consumer backlash? Aurélia fixes herself a coffee, sits down in her beautiful garden not far from Paris and goes on Instagram "to relax." First up: "a guy I like a lot who does interior design. He's in Venice at the moment." She's into interior design, and has even just had two bird drawings by the 19th Century English designer William Morris tattooed on her arms. She scrolls down. Two kittens having a fight. "I love animals so I get a lot of animals. That's how it works, social media. You click on bananas and they give you bananas." There are ads too – although they look just like the other posts – for a robot-vacuum cleaner, a diet and bed linen (with Morris-inspired designs). But no friends. She has 198 on Instagram but she says "it's completely changed. I practically don’t see any friends' posts anymore." She’s pretty much given up posting herself. "I don't think anyone sees them anymore anyway."  While there remain committed social, amateur posters on Instagram and especially Facebook, the switch from communicating with people you know to scrolling through professionally made content from people you don't, is even more pronounced among young users. Kylian, 16, is in vocational training to become a chef. He's on TikTok and Youtube a lot, he says. "I like looking at videos more than photos or messages. I watch videos made by people I don't know. I don’t post at all. I'm a rather shy person. I stay in my bubble. I watch and that’s all. I keep my reactions to myself." "I spend a lot of time scrolling through videos made by content-creators," says Lucie, also 16. "They're more interesting than the posts of people I know." She doesn't post except sometimes "stories" which disappear after 24 hours.  Whether it's TikTok, Snapchat, Facebook and Instagram, we are a long way from the "digital town square" of personal interaction that social media was even just a few years ago. In France, annual official Barometre du numerique 2026  shows 49% of social media users are "active only occasionally". In the UK, an Ofcom report   published in April showed a year-on-year drop of users who actively post from 61% to 49%. In the US, a Morning Consult survey of June last year found 28% reported posting less often than the previous year. Just 33% now post daily compared to 57% who use it for entertainment daily. The gap is a lot wider still for Gen Z – 18% active for 74% passive. Vanessa Lalo, a Paris-based clinical psychologist specialising in on-line behaviour, says "users have become more conscious that the traces you leave (on social media) stay there forever and some no longer want to maintain social media relations that can be superficial. Some don’t want the exposure to criticism that might be a risk when you post or the feeling that their post will seem poor alongside all the professional content". However, Lalo adds, people haven’t stopped posting, rather they are posting different things and in different places. "On TikTok, for example, young people publish a lot of content but it's more funny parodies and remixes of existing material. The goal is to make people laugh, not to tell people about their lives." That still happens, she says, but it’s moved from social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook to messaging sites like WhatsApp. There's also been a move towards private groups on Instagram and Snapchat. "These are much more intimate places where you're not bombarded with ads and content made by influencers," she says. "What we're seeing is social media splitting in two," says social media consultant Matt Navarra, author of the Geekout Newsletter. "Big platforms like Instagram and TikTok are becoming more about entertainment and discovery. WhatsApp is becoming the place people go to actually be social. The catch is, those kinds of spaces are harder for companies to make money from." Small business owners are being pushed to become presenters, editors, trend spotters and content creators, on top of actually running the business – Matt Navarra It was TikTok that helped to pioneer an algorithm that figures out from the moment you start scrolling what you like, and then fills your feed with material calculated to keep you on the app for the longest possible time. Now, says Matt Navarra, "Meta has built what it calls an AI system for unconnected content recommendations on Facebook and Instagram, which basically means, they're increasingly showing you stuff from people you don't follow because the machine thinks you're going to like it. It's not biased towards, is it a professional creator? Is it a brand? Is it a friend? If they can see that you've engaged with a friend a lot, you might see a lot more of their content. It's just that who you are friends with, who you follow, has become irrelevant in a way." This all means that small businesses, that have long used social media for free promotion have to up their game.   "There's a real opportunity for some small businesses," says Matt Navarra. "A bakery, florist, salon or local café can still break through if they have a good story, strong visuals or behind-the-scenes content people want to watch. But it also means the job has changed. Small business owners are being pushed to become presenters, editors, trend spotters and content creators, on top of actually running the business." The social platforms continue to be monetised predominantly by ad revenue. That is still the core business model. And ad revenue continues to grow – Matt Navarra Social media is evolving into something passive like television, albeit television that adapts as you zap. Or rather which knows you so well that it doesn't seem to matter that much that it's taken the remote control. You give the platform information about yourself that it uses for commercial gain and, in return, it gives you content tailored to please you for free. The transition from truly social media to entertainment platform does seem to be paying off. "The social platforms continue to be monetised predominantly by ad revenue. That is still the core business model. And ad revenue continues to grow," says Matt Navarra. Global social media ad revenue is expected to reach $317 billion (£236bn) in 2026, up from $277 billion (£206bn) last year. Meta is the biggest winner. Its ad sales already increased 22% year-on-year in 2025.  Ad sales are expected to hit $243 billion (£181bn) this year , enough to overtake Google for the first time. AI powered digital ad targeting is becoming ever more effective and precise. "The social platforms allow companies to put ads amongst the content that you're scrolling through. Every third or fourth scroll is an ad. And they are the world's best ad targeting engines. They know so much about your interests because of what you've looked at, liked, engaged with, what you've chosen to follow, the time you've spent in certain areas of the app, things like that," Navarra says.  "So advertisers will go in and say: 'I want to place an ad next to people in the UK who are between thirty and sixty years old and who are interested in DIY' and the social platforms will have that information and will place the ads accordingly." The price will depend on the number of impressions (clicks) the advertiser wants and how tight the criteria are. It costs more to place ads in the social media feeds of people who buy horses than people who buy ice-cream. More like this: •  TikTok is tracking you, even if you don't use the app. Here's how to stop it •  How to stop AI from turning your brain to mush •  This monkey selfie will protect you from AI slop Might there be a backlash coming? Don't many people go on to social media to see how friends are reacting to their posts or comments before settling down to scroll through professionally made content? Whether it's the shrinking social motivation to get on these apps or something else, the amount of time people spend on social media plateaued at an average of 141 minutes in 2025, down slightly from 143 minutes in 2024 . However, this is only part of the story, as the number of people using social media and the total time humanity spends on these apps continues to rise. For Gen Z it’s higher still. Around five hours a day in the United States where, for this demographic, social media has also become the primary search engine and shopping tool. Meanwhile, for those who miss what are fast becoming the old days when social media enabled you to share a bit of your life, a joke or a point of view with people you more-or-less knew, there are tools within platforms, says Matt Navarra, that allow you to choose to see mainly friends and family content. "People can flick to a feed that gives them that," he says. "But most people don't." -- If you liked this story, sign up for The Essential List newsletter – a handpicked selection of features, videos and can't-miss news, delivered to your inbox twice a week.   For more on business and beyond, follow us on  LinkedIn . 社交媒体平台曾经用于朋友间的交流——如今许多平台日益成为短视频娱乐中心。其商业模式是增加人们在应用上花费的时间，并提高广告收入。但消费者是否已经出现反弹？

##段落

奥蕾莉亚给自己冲了一杯咖啡，坐在巴黎附近美丽的花园里，打开Instagram“放松一下”。首先映入眼帘的是：“一个我非常喜欢的做室内设计的家伙。他现在在威尼斯。”她对室内设计情有独钟，甚至刚刚把19世纪英国设计师威廉·莫里斯的两幅鸟类画纹在了手臂上。她往下滑动。两只小猫在打架。“我喜欢动物，所以会刷到很多动物内容。社交媒体就是这样运作的。你点击香蕉，它就给你推送香蕉。”还有广告——尽管看起来和其他帖子没什么两样——涉及扫地机器人、减肥餐和床品（带有莫里斯风格的设计）。但看不到朋友。她在Instagram上有198个好友，但她说“情况完全变了。我几乎再也看不到任何朋友的帖子了。”她自己也基本不再发帖了。“我觉得反正也没人会看。”

##段落

虽然在Instagram尤其是Facebook上仍有热衷社交的业余发帖者，但从与认识的人交流转向浏览陌生人的专业制作内容，这一趋势在年轻用户中尤为明显。16岁的基利安正在接受厨师职业培训。他说自己经常刷TikTok和YouTube。“我喜欢看视频胜过看照片或消息。我看的是不认识的人制作的视频。我完全不发帖。我是个比较害羞的人。我待在自己的小圈子里。只看不说话。我把反应藏在心里。”

##段落

“我花很多时间刷内容创作者制作的视频，”同样16岁的露西说。“它们比认识的人的帖子更有趣。”她除了偶尔发一些24小时后消失的“快拍”外，从不发帖。无论是TikTok、Snapchat、Facebook还是Instagram，我们早已远离了社交媒体几年前还是“数字城镇广场”式的个人互动时代。在法国，2026年官方年度《数字晴雨表》显示，49%的社交媒体用户“仅偶尔活跃”。在英国，4月发布的Ofcom报告显示，积极发帖的用户同比下降，从61%降至49%。在美国，去年6月Morning Consult的一项调查发现，28%的受访者表示发帖频率低于前一年。目前只有33%的人每天发帖，而每天使用社交媒体进行娱乐的人比例为57%。在Z世代中，这一差距更加悬殊——18%积极发帖，74%被动浏览。瓦内萨·拉洛，一位驻巴黎的临床心理学家，专攻在线行为研究。

她说：“用户已经越来越意识到，你在社交媒体上留下的痕迹会永远存在，有些人不再愿意维护可能肤浅的社交媒体关系。有些人不想暴露在发帖可能带来的批评风险中，或者担心自己的帖子在众多专业内容中显得逊色。”然而，拉洛补充说，人们并没有停止发帖，而是换了内容和地点。“例如，在TikTok上，年轻人发布大量内容，但更多是对现有素材的有趣模仿和混剪。目标是让人们发笑，而不是分享生活。”她说，分享生活仍然存在，但已从Instagram和Facebook等平台转移到WhatsApp等即时通讯应用。此外，人们也在转向Instagram和Snapchat上的私密群组。“这些是更私密的空间，你不会被广告和网红内容轰炸，”她说。

社交媒体顾问马特·纳瓦拉（Matt Navarra）在《极客通讯》（Geekout Newsletter）中写道：“我们看到社交媒体正在一分为二。像Instagram和TikTok这样的大平台越来越侧重于娱乐和发现。WhatsApp则成为人们真正社交的地方。问题是，这类空间更难让企业获利。”小型企业主被迫成为主持人、编辑、潮流观察者和内容创作者，同时还要实际经营业务——马特·纳瓦拉。

正是TikTok率先开创了一种算法，从你开始滚动屏幕的那一刻就能判断你喜欢什么，然后填充你的信息流，以计算出的内容让你在应用上停留尽可能长的时间。现在，马特·纳瓦拉说，“Meta已经在其Facebook和Instagram上构建了一个所谓的AI系统，用于非关联内容推荐，这基本上意味着，它们越来越倾向于向你展示你不关注的人的内容，因为机器认为你会喜欢。它不偏向于是否专业创作者、品牌或朋友。如果它看到你和某个朋友互动很多，你可能会看到更多他们的内容。只是，你的朋友是谁、你关注谁，在某种程度上已经变得无关紧要。”这一切意味着，长期利用社交媒体进行免费推广的小型企业必须提升自己的水平。

“对于一些小企业来说，确实存在机会，”马特·纳瓦拉说。“面包店、花店、沙龙或本地咖啡馆，如果有好故事、强视觉或人们想看的幕后内容，仍然可以脱颖而出。但这也意味着工作方式已经改变。小型企业主被迫成为主持人、编辑、潮流观察者和内容创作者，同时还要实际经营业务。”

##段落
真正经营业务的核心部分。"社交平台仍然主要通过广告收入实现商业化，这依然是核心商业模式，且广告收入持续增长——马特·纳瓦拉。社交媒体正演变为一种类似电视的被动媒介，尽管是那种会随着你切换频道而适应的电视，或者更确切地说，是一种对你如此了解，以至于它拿走遥控器这件事似乎也没那么重要的电视。你向平台提供关于自己的信息，平台利用这些信息获取商业利益，作为回报，它免费为你提供量身定制的取悦内容。从真正的社交媒体向娱乐平台的转变似乎确实在奏效。"社交平台仍然主要通过广告收入实现商业化，这依然是核心商业模式，且广告收入持续增长，"马特·纳瓦拉表示。全球社交媒体广告收入预计将从去年的2770亿美元（2060亿英镑）增长至2026年的3170亿美元（2360亿英镑）。Meta是最大的赢家，其2025年广告销售额已同比增长22%，预计今年将达到2430亿美元（1810亿英镑），足以首次超越谷歌。AI驱动的数字广告定向投放正变得前所未有的高效和精准。"社交平台允许企业在你浏览的内容中插入广告，每滚动三四次就会出现一条广告。它们是全球最优秀的广告定向引擎，因为你的浏览记录、点赞、互动、关注选择、在应用特定区域停留的时间等信息，它们对你的兴趣了如指掌，"纳瓦拉说。"因此广告主会说：'我想把广告投放给英国30至60岁、对DIY感兴趣的人群'，社交平台掌握这些信息，就会相应地进行广告投放。"价格取决于广告主想要的曝光次数（点击量）以及筛选条件的严格程度。将广告投放到购买马匹的人群的社交媒体信息流中，比投放到购买冰淇淋的人群要花费更多。

##段落
更多类似内容：• TikTok正在追踪你，即使你不使用该应用，以下是阻止方法 • 如何防止AI让你的大脑变得迟钝 • 这张猴子自拍照将保护你免受AI垃圾内容的侵害

##段落
是否会有反弹出现？难道不是很多人先上社交媒体看看朋友对自己的帖子或评论有何反应，然后才安下心来浏览专业制作的内容吗？无论是使用这些应用的社交动力减弱还是其他原因，人们在社交媒体上花费的时间在2025年趋于平稳，平均为141分钟，略低于2024年的143分钟。然而，这只是故事的一部分，因为使用社交媒体的人数

##段落  
人工智能以及人类在这些应用上花费的总时间持续增长。对于Z世代而言，这一数字更高。在美国，这一群体每天约花费五小时，社交媒体已成为他们的主要搜索引擎和购物工具。与此同时，对于那些怀念社交媒体刚兴起时、能与熟人分享生活点滴、笑话或观点的人，平台内也有工具可选，马特·纳瓦拉表示，用户可以选择主要查看朋友和家人的内容。他说：“人们可以切换到那种信息流，但大多数人并不这么做。”——如果你喜欢这个故事，请订阅《必读清单》新闻通讯，每周两次精选专题、视频和不可错过的新闻，直接发送到你的邮箱。如需更多商业及其他领域内容，请在领英上关注我们。商业科技专题社交媒体商业世界

readings.title: The bears cooling off in a California pool
body: 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Isabelle Gerretsen Black bears love lounging in Brian Gordon and Ricardo Martinez's pool in Los Angeles. As bear encounters increase across Southern California, the couple share videos of their furry visitors and reveal how they are co-existing with these wild animals. When Brian Gordon first learned that black bears were swimming in the pool of the house he was buying in Los Angeles, he was very afraid. "I'd never seen a bear in real life. I said, 'We'll just build a big wall with barbed wire,'" he recalls. Four years later, Gordon loves nothing more than seeing a family of bears playing in his pool and running around his garden. The furry visitors stop by several times a week. (Scroll down to watch a video of the bears at play.) "They are fine to come here and scratch on the trees, take a nap, and jump in the pool if it's hot, as long as we're not creating harm for them, or for ourselves," Gordon says. Gordon and his partner Ricardo Martinez have made it their mission to peacefully share their pool and garden with the bears. But behind these charming videos of bears relaxing in their pool, there's a deeper story of vigilance and safety precautions that make this co-existence possible. The couple live in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, in Southern California, home to around 1,600 bears . Their house is in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and borders the Angeles National Forest, which spans 700,000 acres (2,830sq km). When the couple moved in, they started spotting bears almost immediately. They initially tried to chase the bears away by yelling, using air horns and occasionally a paintball gun with soft rubber pellets. "But it felt horrible," says Martinez. "It did not sit right with us. We said that as long as they're not breaking into the home and getting into the trash, then they're ok to come by." They sought an approach that would keep both themselves and the bears safe, despite close proximity. "We've since settled on less aggressive means, and honestly, they work better for us," says Gordon. We have had bears crashing barbecues – Brian Gordon Martinez says that black bears are "misunderstood". "They are not going to eat you," says Martinez. Black bear attacks are incredibly rare, with just one fatal attack recorded in California's history .  The couple say they always keep a "healthy distance" from the bears and stay inside when the animals are around. There are sometimes unplanned encounters though.  "We have had bears crashing barbecues," says Gordon. "But if they see you, they usually just walk away." Gordon and Martinez say their favourite bear visitor is Maddie, who they first got to know as an incredibly inquisitive youngster in 2023. She loved playing in the pool and hanging around the garden. "She is our golden child," says Martinez. A year later, Maddie returned with her cubs in tow. "Unfortunately she lost those cubs, so we went through an emotional rollercoaster with her," says Martinez. This year she has brought her new cubs to the house. "They're the most adorable [creatures] you've ever seen. They're so cuddly but also intimidating, with their long claws." We live here and the bears live here. We don't want them to go anywhere – Ricardo Martinez Punky is another "rambunctious yearling" who first came to the house as a cub with her mother, says Gordon. "She would pop all the pool floaties." She once climbed onto an inflatable cupcake and drifted into the middle of the pool. "She really stole our hearts that summer with her pool fun," says Gordon. They nicknamed another regular visitor "Nappy", as the female bear likes to take long siestas while floating in the pool. "She'll literally go to the steps of the pool, get in and put her head down. She's the only bear I've seen take hour-long naps in the pool," says Gordon. If she sees the couple, Nappy will huff at them. "She's a big mama bear and she's just a little grumpy about everything in life," Gordon jokes. These characters are among a growing number of black bears trying to make a home alongside Californians , and often posing challenges for local communities.  There are more than 60,000 black bears living in California , says Wilson Sherman, a research fellow at the University of California, Los Angeles. Black bears are an increasingly common sight in LA suburbs. "They are really intelligent, adaptable omnivores. They eat everything and have learned how to gain calories in places where people live," says Sherman, who studies how communities respond to black bears.  Not all bear encounters are as positive as Gordon and Martinez's experience though. "We do see incidents pretty regularly of bears raiding trash and entering homes," says Sherman. "The really sad thing about this is that when things go awry, it's usually the bears that end up paying the price. Several bears have been put down in the last few years.   A mother black bear called Blondie was euthanised by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife in March 2026 after she swiped at a woman walking her dog in Monrovia.  Blondie had also visited Gordon and Martinez's garden a few times and never caused any problems. Gordon organised a petition to try to prevent the euthanasia, which was signed by almost 6,000 people. "It was pretty devastating. Blondie resembles all mama bears, just trying to find shelter, to raise her kids and live her life," he says. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife says that DNA testing revealed that the captured bear was responsible for the incident, as well as a previous attack on an elderly resident sitting on his porch in Monrovia in June 2025. "Euthanasia is used only as a last resort when an animal poses a risk to public safety and cannot be safely returned to the wild," says a spokesperson. "Relocation may seem like a solution but is not an option when it could put public safety at risk. Bears have strong spatial memory and often return to familiar areas." The bear's cubs are being cared for at a wildlife rehabilitation centre and will be released into a suitable habitat when they are ready, he adds. To minimise conflict with bears, Sherman says it is important that communities restrict access to attractants, such as rubbish bins and leaving food outdoors.  "For a bear, finding a box that's full of pizza when you've been spending your time digging for worms and roots is a game changer." Keeping neighbourhoods bear-free is a "collective training effort", Sherman adds. "You all have to be on the same page, because if one person's leaving a lot of really good stuff in their yard, the bear is very likely going to think, 'I should check out a handful of other yards.'" Gordon says that they are "hypervigilant" when it comes to waste. "We don't even use our trash cans. I haul it to my office, a couple of times a week." They also keep their doors and windows closed and don't ever leave food in their car. They're not teddy bears, they are still wild animals – Wilson Sherman The couple say they have never had a negative encounter with any of the bears visiting their home. Martinez once found Nappy in the garage when he'd accidentally left it open. "We both startled each other," he says. "I slowly walked back, because you don't ever want to corner a bear." She emerged from the garage and went on her way, he says. More like this:
Why grizzly bears need their own hiking trails
The true story of Germany ' s rampant raccoons

Social media accounts, like Martinez and Gordon's, and home surveillance cameras are allowing people "to understand bears as individuals and providing an intimate look into their lives", says Sherman. But he has some reservations. "There's always the risk of Disneyfication, of painting too fuzzy a picture. They're not teddy bears, they are still wild animals." Sherman warns that it is important that bears and humans don't become too comfortable around each other. "Part of loving bears is creating healthy boundaries and setting the bears up for success when they inevitably pass through our neighbourhoods," he says. Through their Instagram account dedicated to the bears, @poolbearlife, Gordon and Martinez hope to raise awareness of how people can behave safely around bears and how to mitigate unwanted encounters. They stress that their relationship with black bears is not something that could necessarily be universal. "This works for us, for where we live," says Gordon.  "It's all about finding that balance with wildlife, how can we co-thrive?" says Martinez. "We live here and the bears live here. We don't want them to go anywhere." -- For essential climate news and hopeful developments to your inbox, sign up to the  Future Earth newsletter, while  The Essential List delivers a handpicked selection of features and insights twice a week.   For more science, technology, environment and health stories from the BBC, follow us on  Facebook and  Instagram . ##段落
三天前 分享 保存 设为Google首选 伊莎贝尔·杰勒特森 黑熊喜欢在洛杉矶布莱恩·戈登和里卡多·马丁内斯的泳池里消遣。随着南加州熊出没事件日益增多，这对夫妇分享了他们毛茸茸访客的视频，并透露了他们如何与这些野生动物共存。

##段落
当布莱恩·戈登第一次得知黑熊在他正打算购买的洛杉矶房子里游泳时，他非常害怕。“我从未在现实生活中见过熊。我说，‘我们干脆建一堵带铁丝网的高墙吧，’”他回忆道。四年后，戈登最爱的莫过于看着一家熊在他的泳池里玩耍、在花园里跑来跑去。这些毛茸茸的访客每周都会光顾好几次。（向下滚动观看熊玩耍的视频。）“它们来这里抓抓树、打个盹、天热了跳进泳池，完全没问题，只要我们不伤害它们，也不伤害我们自己，”戈登说。

##段落
戈登和他的伴侣里卡多·马丁内斯把与熊和平共享泳池和花园视为自己的使命。但在这些熊在泳池中放松的迷人视频背后，是一个关于警惕和安全防范的更深层故事，正是这些让共存成为可能。

##段落
这对夫妇住在南加州洛杉矶县蒙罗维亚，那里是大约1600只熊的家园。他们的房子位于圣盖博山脉山麓，紧邻占地70万英亩（2830平方公里）的安吉利斯国家森林。夫妇俩搬进来后，几乎立刻就发现了熊的踪迹。他们起初试图通过大喊大叫、使用气喇叭，偶尔用装有软橡胶弹丸的彩弹枪来驱赶熊。“但那感觉糟透了，”马丁内斯说。“我们心里过意不去。我们说，只要它们不闯进屋里、不翻垃圾桶，那它们来转转就没问题。”他们寻求一种既能保证自身安全又能保护熊的方法，尽管彼此距离很近。“我们后来采用了不那么激进的手段，老实说，这对我们更有效，”戈登说。

##段落
我们遇到过熊闯入烧烤现场的情况——布莱恩·戈登 马丁内斯说黑熊“被误解了”。“它们不会吃掉你的，”马丁内斯说。黑熊袭击事件极为罕见，加州历史上仅记录过一例致命袭击。这对夫妇表示，他们始终与熊保持“安全距离”，当动物在附近时，他们就待在室内。不过有时也会发生意外相遇。“我们遇到过熊闯入烧烤现场的情况，”戈登说。“但如果它们看到你，通常只会走开。”戈登和马丁内斯说，他们最喜欢的熊访客是麦迪，他们最初在2023年认识她时，她还是一只极其好奇的小熊。她喜欢在泳池里玩耍，喜欢在周围闲逛。

##段落
“她是我们的金孩子，”马丁内斯说。一年后，玛蒂带着她的幼崽回来了。“不幸的是，她失去了那些幼崽，所以我们和她一起经历了情绪上的过山车，”马丁内斯说。今年，她带着新生的幼崽来到了房子。“它们是你见过的最可爱的[生物]。它们非常惹人喜爱，但也令人畏惧，因为它们有长长的爪子。”我们住在这里，熊也住在这里。我们不想让它们去任何地方——里卡多·马丁内斯

##段落
Punky是另一只“精力充沛的一岁熊”，戈登说，她最初是作为幼崽和母亲一起来到房子的。“她会把所有的泳池浮具都弄破。”她曾经爬上一个充气蛋糕，漂到泳池中央。“那个夏天，她在泳池里的乐趣真的俘获了我们的心，”戈登说。他们给另一位常客起了个绰号叫“纳皮”，因为这只母熊喜欢在泳池里漂浮时打长长的午盹。“她真的会走到泳池台阶边，进去，把头低下。她是我见过的唯一一只在泳池里打一小时盹的熊，”戈登说。如果她看到这对夫妇，纳皮会朝他们喷气。“她是个熊妈妈，对生活中的一切都有点暴躁，”戈登开玩笑说。

##段落
这些角色是越来越多的黑熊试图与加州人共同安家的一部分，它们经常给当地社区带来挑战。加州大学洛杉矶分校的研究员威尔逊·谢尔曼说，加州生活着超过6万只黑熊。黑熊在洛杉矶郊区越来越常见。“它们是非常聪明、适应性强的杂食动物。它们什么都吃，并且学会了如何在人类居住的地方获取卡路里，”研究社区如何应对黑熊的谢尔曼说。

##段落
并非所有与熊的相遇都像戈登和马丁内斯的经历那样积极。“我们确实经常看到熊翻垃圾和闯入房屋的事件，”谢尔曼说。“真正可悲的是，当事情出错时，通常最终付出代价的是熊。过去几年里，有几只熊被处死了。”一只名叫布隆迪的母黑熊在2026年3月于蒙罗维亚抓伤一名遛狗的女性后，被加州鱼类和野生动物部门实施安乐死。布隆迪也曾几次造访戈登和马丁内斯的花园，从未造成任何问题。戈登组织了一份请愿书，试图阻止安乐死，有近6000人签名。“这非常令人心碎。布隆迪和所有熊妈妈一样，只是在试图寻找庇护所，抚养孩子，过自己的生活，”他说。加州鱼类和野生动物部门表示，DNA测试证实，被捕获的熊对这起事件以及之前的一起事件负有责任。

2025年6月，蒙罗维亚一位年长居民坐在自家门廊时遭到袭击。“安乐死仅在动物对公共安全构成风险且无法安全放归野外时，作为最后手段使用，”一位发言人表示。“搬迁看似是解决方案，但当可能危及公共安全时，这并非选项。熊具有强烈的空间记忆，往往会返回熟悉的区域。”他补充说，这只熊的幼崽正在野生动物康复中心接受照料，待时机成熟后将放归适宜的栖息地。谢尔曼表示，为尽量减少与熊的冲突，社区限制接触诱因（如垃圾桶和户外遗留食物）至关重要。“对一只熊来说，当你一直在挖蠕虫和树根为食时，发现一个装满披萨的盒子简直是改变命运的事。”保持社区无熊是一项“集体训练努力”，谢尔曼补充道。“所有人都必须达成共识，因为如果一个人院子里留了大量好东西，熊很可能想，‘我应该去检查其他几个院子。’”戈登表示，他们在垃圾处理方面“高度警惕”。“我们甚至不用自家的垃圾桶。我每周几次把垃圾运到办公室。”他们还保持门窗关闭，并且从不将食物留在车内。它们不是泰迪熊，它们仍然是野生动物——威尔逊·谢尔曼这对夫妇表示，他们从未与到访家中的任何熊有过负面接触。马丁内斯曾有一次不小心让车库门开着，发现纳皮在里面。“我们互相吓了一跳，”他说。“我慢慢后退，因为你永远不想困住一只熊。”他说，她从车库出来，然后离开了。更多类似内容：
为什么灰熊需要自己的徒步小径
看到熊时该怎么办
德国浣熊泛滥的真实故事谢尔曼表示，像马丁内斯和戈登这样的社交媒体账号以及家庭监控摄像头，让人们“将熊视为个体，并得以亲密一窥它们的生活”。但他有些保留意见。“总有迪士尼化的风险，把画面描绘得过于温馨。它们不是泰迪熊，它们仍然是野生动物。”谢尔曼警告说，熊和人类彼此过于舒适相处是危险的。“爱熊的一部分在于建立健康的界限，并确保熊在不可避免地经过我们社区时能够顺利生存，”他说。通过他们专门记录熊的Instagram账号@poolbearlife，戈登和马丁内斯希望提高人们对如何在熊周围安全行为以及如何减少不必要遭遇的认识。他们强调，他们与黑熊的关系是

这未必是放之四海而皆准的做法。戈登说：“这对我们有效，适合我们生活的地方。”马丁内斯说：“关键在于找到与野生动物共存的平衡点，我们如何共同繁荣？”“我们住在这里，熊也住在这里。我们不希望它们去任何地方。”——如需获取关键气候新闻和有希望的进展，请订阅《未来地球》简报，而《要闻清单》每周两次为您精选专题和见解。欲了解更多BBC科学、技术、环境和健康报道，请在Facebook和Instagram上关注我们。地球 野生动物 自然与户外 环境 热浪 专题 熊

readings.title: The Supreme Court just gave Trump his illegal ballroom
body: Politics The Supreme Court just gave Trump his illegal ballroom And the justices didn’t even bother to explain why… by Ian Millhiser Aug 31, 2026, 9:45 PM UTC Gift President Donald Trump talks to reporters on May 19, 2026 about his proposed White House ballroom next to what used to be the East Wing. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images Ian Millhiser is a senior correspondent at Vox, where he focuses on the Supreme Court, the Constitution, and the decline of liberal democracy in the United States. He received a JD from Duke University and is the author of two books on the Supreme Court. Welp, the Supreme Court has decided that President Donald Trump gets to build his ballroom. The decision in National Park Service v. National Trust for Historic Preservation is 5-4, with Republican Chief Justice John Roberts joining the three Democratic justices in dissent. Notably, no member of the Court argued that Trump’s ballroom, an enormous structure that the president plans to build on the former site of the White House’s East Wing, is legal. As Roberts points out in dissent, a federal law prohibits the construction of any “building or structure … on any reservation, park, or public grounds of the Federal Government in the District of Columbia without express authority of Congress.” And, as Roberts writes, “Congress has not passed any law resembling ‘express authority’ for the Executive’s construction of” Trump’s ballroom. Email (required) Sign Up By submitting your email, you agree to our Terms and Privacy Notice . This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply. Nevertheless, the five Republicans in the majority manage to rule in favor of Trump by effectively immunizing his ballroom from federal lawsuits. Their opinion highlights two of the most troubling things about the current Supreme Court: its reluctance to impose limits on Trump’s imperial-style presidency, and the frequent incoherence of its reasoning, especially in Trump cases. Their opinion suggests that no one is allowed to sue to challenge Trump’s decision to destroy and replace much of the White House. But it is short, does not explain key points of its argument, and relies on several distinctions that do not make any sense. As a general rule, no one is allowed to file a federal lawsuit unless they can show that they were injured in some way by the defendant they are suing — a requirement known as “standing.” But the Court has long held that plaintiffs suing under conservationist laws that seek to preserve a pristine, sacred, historical, or otherwise beautiful site have standing to bring a suit enforcing such laws against defendants who would damage or destroy such a site’s beauty. In Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife (1992), for example, the Court said that “the desire to use or observe an animal species, even for purely esthetic purposes, is undeniably a cognizable interest” that can be asserted in federal court. Similarly, the Court held in Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw Environmental Services (2000) that “environmental plaintiffs adequately allege injury in fact when they aver that they use the affected area and are persons ‘for whom the aesthetic and recreational values of the area will be lessened’ by the challenged activity.’” So that’s how standing worked right up until Monday afternoon, when the Court handed down its latest opinion. The new rule is…well, it is difficult to parse. The plaintiff in National Park Service is a conservationist organization whose members include a retired professor who would frequently walk by the White House and who admired its beauty. Under decisions like Lujan and Friends of the Earth , that was enough to give her standing to sue in order to challenge the ballroom. The five Republicans in the majority, however, falsely claim that this individual merely argued that she is offended by Trump’s construction project, and that past decisions have involved “more than mere offense.” The Republicans note that, in Friends of the Earth , the plaintiffs not only wanted to view a river, but also to fish and swim in it and to camp nearby. But they don’t really even attempt to distinguish Lujan beyond a vague statement that Lujan requires a plaintiff’s injury to be “concrete and particularized.” Thus, because the majority opinion is so poorly explained, it is hard to tell what its implications will be. If the Court had explicitly overruled its past decisions holding that a plaintiff may often sue to challenge the destruction of something beautiful, that would be an existential threat to countless environmental, conservationist, and historical preservation laws that all exist to preserve natural or historic beauty. But the Court’s failure to explain why Lujan does not require them to rule against Trump leaves lawyers and judges to guess at what the Court just did to the rules governing standing. Perhaps this is a one-off decision intended solely to do a favor for Trump. Or maybe it’s the harbinger of a future decision setting much of America’s environmental protection regime on fire . The five justices in the majority barely explain themselves, so we cannot yet know what National Park Service means. But one thing that is clear is that the decision makes no sense. As Roberts writes in dissent, “it now is the case that ‘I want to look at a crocodile’ can adequately answer the ever-critical ‘what’s it to you?’ question of Article III standing, while ‘I want to look at the White House’ cannot.” But the justices in the majority couldn’t even be bothered to explain why. ##段落
政治 最高法院刚刚给了特朗普他的非法舞厅 而大法官们甚至懒得解释为什么……作者：伊恩·米尔希瑟 2026年8月31日，晚上9:45 UTC 赠品 2026年5月19日，总统唐纳德·特朗普在原本是东翼的位置旁，就其提议的白宫舞厅向记者讲话。Chip Somodevilla/盖蒂图片社 伊恩·米尔希瑟是Vox的高级记者，专注于最高法院、美国宪法以及美国自由民主的衰退。他拥有杜克大学的法学博士学位，并著有关于最高法院的两本书。

##段落
唉，最高法院已经决定唐纳德·特朗普总统可以建造他的舞厅。国家公园管理局诉国家历史保护信托案中的裁决是5比4，共和党首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨加入了三位民主党大法官的反对意见。值得注意的是，法院没有任何成员认为特朗普的舞厅——总统计划在前白宫东翼旧址上建造的巨型建筑——是合法的。正如罗伯茨在反对意见中指出的，联邦法律禁止“在哥伦比亚特区联邦政府的任何保留地、公园或公共场地上，未经国会明确授权建造任何‘建筑或结构’。”而且，正如罗伯茨所写，“国会没有通过任何类似于‘明确授权’的法律，来允许行政部门建造”特朗普的舞厅。

##段落

##段落
尽管如此，多数派中的五位共和党人设法通过有效地使特朗普的舞厅免受联邦诉讼来支持特朗普。他们的意见凸显了当前最高法院最令人不安的两点：它不愿对特朗普帝国式总统任期施加限制，以及其推理经常缺乏连贯性，尤其是在特朗普相关案件中。他们的意见表明，没有人可以起诉质疑特朗普摧毁并替换白宫大部分建筑的决定。但该意见篇幅简短，没有解释其论证的关键点，并依赖于几个毫无意义的区分。

##段落
一般而言，除非原告能证明他们因所起诉的被告而以某种方式受到伤害，否则不允许提起联邦诉讼——这一要求被称为“诉讼资格”。但法院长期以来一直认为，根据旨在保护原始、神圣、历史或其他美丽地点的保护主义法律提起诉讼的原告，具有诉讼资格，可以提起执行此类法律以对抗会损害或摧毁该地点之美的被告。例如，在卢汉诉野生动物保护者案（1992）中，法院表示“

##段落
渴望使用或观察某一动物物种，即便是纯粹出于审美目的，也无疑是一种可认定的利益，可以在联邦法院中主张。同样，法院在“地球之友诉莱德劳环境服务公司”（2000年）一案中裁定，“环境原告在声称使用受影响区域，且是‘该区域审美与休闲价值因被质疑活动而降低’的人时，即充分指控了事实上的伤害。”这就是直到周一下午法院发布最新意见之前，诉讼资格（standing）的运作方式。而新规则……嗯，很难解读。

##段落
“国家公园服务案”中的原告是一个环保组织，其成员包括一位退休教授，她经常路过白宫并欣赏其美景。根据“卢汉案”和“地球之友案”等判决，这足以赋予她起诉以挑战舞厅建设项目的资格。然而，占多数的五位共和党法官错误地声称，该个人仅主张她对特朗普的建设项目感到冒犯，而过去的判决涉及“不仅仅是单纯的冒犯”。共和党人指出，在“地球之友案”中，原告不仅想观赏河流，还想在其中钓鱼、游泳并在附近露营。但他们甚至没有真正尝试区分“卢汉案”，只是模糊地表示“卢汉案”要求原告的伤害必须是“具体且特定的”。

##段落
因此，由于多数意见解释得如此糟糕，很难判断其影响将是什么。如果法院明确推翻了过去认定原告常可起诉以挑战破坏美的事物的判决，那将对无数旨在保护自然或历史美景的环境法、环保法和历史保护法构成生存威胁。但法院未能解释为何“卢汉案”不要求他们裁定特朗普败诉，这让律师和法官只能猜测法院刚刚对诉讼资格规则做了什么。

##段落
也许这是一个仅为了给特朗普帮忙而作出的临时性决定。又或者，它是未来判决的先兆，可能点燃美国大部分环境保护体系。占多数的五位法官几乎没有解释自己，所以我们尚无法知道“国家公园服务案”意味着什么。但有一点是明确的：这一判决毫无道理。正如罗伯茨在异议中所写，“现在的情况是，‘我想看鳄鱼’可以充分回答第三条诉讼资格中至关重要的‘关你什么事？’问题，而‘我想看白宫’却不行。”但占多数的法官们甚至懒得解释为什么。

readings.title: The search for a vaccine against Lyme disease
body: 16 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Brianna Abbott Lyme disease is on the rise. But scientists are searching for ways to prevent it. Each time I pull out a wriggling tick from my dog's fur, I flash back to my own brush with Lyme disease – a bacterial infection spread via tick bites. I never found the deer tick that bit me, but I remember the flu-like chills, the body aches and signature bullseye rash that ran up and down my arm. A month of intense antibiotics cleared the infection and I haven’t had any further problems, but other people aren't so lucky. In addition to an oval or circular rash, Lyme disease can cause flu-like symptoms. Infections that go untreated in the short term can lead to potentially debilitating issues in the months and years that follow, such as fatigue, body aches or nerve damage. Meanwhile, there are an estimated 476,000 cases of Lyme disease diagnosed in the US every year – and as ticks expand their territory , that risk is growing. In the US, there are currently no licensed vaccines to prevent Lyme disease in people – but that might be about to change. And scientists are developing other strategies to help prevent infections, too. This is the battle against a group of particularly resilient bacteria and their spider-like host – and it's heating up.   Pfizer released data in March 2026 showing that a four-dose regimen of their novel vaccine was more than 70% effective in preventing Lyme disease in humans "We are seeing many more patients, many more people actually getting infected," says Thomas Hart, assistant professor of molecular microbiology and immunology at Johns Hopkins Lyme and Tickborne Diseases Research and Education Institute, Maryland. "It's a good time for there to be a new preventative." Tick populations are expanding their range throughout Europe and the US , thanks to expanding forest and deer populations and climate change creating milder winters. And while tick season usually stretches from spring to autumn in many places, climate change is now increasingly leading to longer, sometimes year-round tick activity .    Ticks carry a number of pathogens that can infect people, leading to diseases that include encephalitis, anaplasmosis and babesiosis, among others. But Lyme disease, caused by some types of Borrelia bacteria , is the most common tick-related illness in Europe and North America. To this day my labrador Walter continues bounding around in long grass, unscathed by the illnesses ticks carry. He is vaccinated against Lyme disease and eats his monthly chewable tablet, smothered in spray cheese, to ward off fleas, ticks and heartworm – a disease spread via mosquito bites. Currently there are several anti-tick treatments for dogs and cats, which often rely on chemicals that kill ticks once they start to feed. Typically these are either applied directly to the skin as a " spot-on" treatment, disseminated via a collar, or delivered as a tablet .   Developing preventative drugs for humans, on the other hand, is no easy task. Studies in people are harder and more costly to run than those in animals. For trials in people, scientists often need to recruit a large number of participants and follow them over time as they go about their lives. That's because only a small fraction of them will get bitten and develop a tick-borne disease, and there need to be enough infections to show if the vaccine or drug works. In animal trials, meanwhile, researchers often put infected ticks directly on them, almost ensuring that they will get infected with a given tick-borne pathogen, making the trials easier to do. But scientists hesitate to use so-called challenge trials for Lyme disease in people, in part because they don't want to risk giving people lingering, long-term symptoms from the disease. "I don't think anyone would sign up for Lyme," says Linden Hu, professor of immunology at Tufts University School of Medicine in Massachusetts, who has worked with several companies on anti-tick strategies for humans. He explains this is why it's hard to get them approved. There was, however, a human Lyme disease vaccine approved in the US in 1998, called LYMErix. The shot was tested in a trial with more than 10,000 participants and had 76% efficacy in preventing the disease. But demand was low, partly because of reports and lawsuits over side effects, namely arthritis. Health officials reviewed the data in 2002 and didn't find evidence of a safety risk. Still, the vaccine's maker discontinued the shot the same year, citing a lack of demand. Now, the growing number of people at risk of tick-borne diseases has spurred a newfound investment in prevention. In particular, the search for another vaccine against Lyme disease is gathering pace – and starting to yield results. So far, the vaccine candidate that's the furthest along is PF-07307405, by Pfizer and Valneva. It shares a similar target with the old LYMErix vaccine and the shots designed for dogs – a piece of a protein called OspA on the surface of the Lyme disease-causing Borrelia burgdorferi bacterium. The shot prompts a person's immune system to create antibodies against six common versions of OspA found in the US and Europe. Then, when an infected tick bites the person and feeds on blood, it also takes in the person's antibodies. Inside the tick, the antibodies latch onto OspA, blocking the bacteria from leaving the critter. "Your antibodies are able to fight off the bacteria when it's still inside of the tick, preventing infection in the first place," Hart says. Earlier this year, Pfizer announced the results from a phase 3 trial – where scientists test how a new intervention compares with existing ones or a placebo and check its safety. In this case, the trial involved more than 9,400 people, revealing that a four-dose regimen was more than 70% effective in preventing Lyme disease. Fewer participants developed Lyme disease during the trial than expected, however, which meant results wasn’t quite as conclusive as the team had hoped. No major safety concerns were detected, and Pfizer said in a press release that it is confident in the vaccine's potential and plans on submitting it to US government regulators for potential approval.  "I will definitely get it as soon as it's available," says Laura Goodman, an assistant professor and emerging infectious diseases researcher at Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine, New York. Similarly, Moderna is testing two Lyme disease vaccines that target OspA. Both are in phase 2 trials – where an intervention is tested on a larger group of people than in phase 1, to see if it's safe and how well it might work. Meanwhile, researchers at Yale University are investigating a shot that prompts the immune system to respond to tick saliva . This one has not yet been trialled in humans.   Another option is to skip the vaccine altogether. For more than a decade, Mark Klempner, a professor of medicine at UMass Chan Medical School, Massachusetts, has been developing an injection designed to target OspA. While a vaccine works by triggering the immune system to create antibodies, this delivers pre-made antibodies directly into a person. It takes just two days to absorb enough to be protected for four months. Lyme disease is not found everywhere that there are ticks. It's rare to catch it in the southeastern US , for example, where ticks prefer to bite lizards over mammals. The idea behind the injection is that people who live, work or travel in areas with Lyme disease could get it at the beginning of tick season, Klempner says, plus a second dose later on. The product is known as TNX-4800, and has already made it through phase 1 clinical trials, where an intervention is tested to find a safe dose and identify potential side effects. Tonix Pharmaceuticals licensed it in 2025 and plans on launching a phase 2 clinical trial next year, according to the company website . More like this: •  How scientists are closing in on the virus's 'weak spots' •  The rare people who are invulnerable to HIV •  Why do mosquitoes bite some people more than others? Another pharmaceutical company, Tarsus Pharmaceuticals, meanwhile, is working on a pill that deploys the same ingredient as an anti-tick medication for dogs. The drug TP-05 interferes with the ticks' nervous systems and kills them quickly, hopefully before they have time to transmit Lyme disease-causing bacteria and other pathogens. In canines, the drug comes in the form of a chewable tablet, but in people it will be a pill. In March this year, Tarsus announced that it had started a phase 2 clinical trial in people, with results expected in the first half of next year.   "I think it's going to be a game-changer," says Durland Fish, a professor emeritus of epidemiology at Yale School of Public Health, Connecticut, who has researched vector-borne diseases including Lyme disease for decades. The pill could also prevent other rising tick-borne diseases including babesiosis and anaplasmosis, he says. But it's unclear when and if these options will become available. In the meantime, the best prevention is to stop tick bites in the first place . That means staying out of tall grass, wearing protective clothing, and showering and checking for ticks after coming inside. Those tried-and-true methods really work, Hu says, but they can be hard for people to do. "People get tired or are out late at night, the kids are cranky," Hu says. That's where a vaccine or pill that people can take – but don't have to remember every time they go outside – could "really be a public health benefit," he says. – For trusted insights on health and wellbeing, sign up to the Health Fix newsletter by senior health correspondent Melissa Hogenboom who also writes the Live Well For Longer and Six Steps to Calm courses.   For more science, technology, environment and health stories from the BBC, follow us on Facebook and Instagram .  Health Vaccine Science Features

16小时前 分享 保存 设为谷歌首选 Brianna Abbott 莱姆病发病率正在上升。但科学家们正在寻找预防方法。每次我从狗狗的毛发中拉出一只扭动的蜱虫时，都会回想起自己与莱姆病的遭遇——这是一种通过蜱虫叮咬传播的细菌感染。我从未找到那只叮咬我的鹿蜱，但我记得流感般的寒战、全身酸痛，以及手臂上上下下蔓延的标志性靶心状皮疹。一个月的强力抗生素清除了感染，此后我没有再出现任何问题，但其他人就没那么幸运了。除了椭圆形或圆形皮疹外，莱姆病还会引起流感样症状。短期内未接受治疗的感染可能在数月或数年后导致潜在的衰弱性问题，如疲劳、全身酸痛或神经损伤。与此同时，美国每年估计有476,000例莱姆病确诊病例——随着蜱虫扩大活动范围，这一风险正在增长。目前美国尚无获准用于预防人类莱姆病的疫苗——但这种情况可能即将改变。科学家们也在开发其他策略来帮助预防感染。这是与一组特别顽强的细菌及其蜘蛛状宿主的战斗——而且这场战斗正在升温。辉瑞公司于2026年3月发布的数据显示，其新型疫苗的四剂方案在预防人类莱姆病方面的有效性超过70%。

##段落
“我们看到越来越多的患者，越来越多的人实际上被感染，”马里兰州约翰霍普金斯大学莱姆病和蜱传疾病研究与教育研究所分子微生物学和免疫学助理教授托马斯·哈特说。“现在是推出新预防措施的好时机。”由于森林和鹿群数量的扩大以及气候变化导致冬季变暖，蜱虫种群正在欧洲和美国各地扩展其活动范围。虽然蜱虫季节在许多地方通常从春季持续到秋季，但气候变化现在日益导致蜱虫活动时间更长，有时甚至全年活跃。

##段落
蜱虫携带多种可感染人类的病原体，导致脑炎、无形体病和巴贝虫病等疾病。但由某些类型的伯氏疏螺旋体细菌引起的莱姆病，是欧洲和北美最常见的蜱传疾病。至今，我的拉布拉多犬沃尔特仍在长草中欢快地蹦跳，毫发无损地躲过了蜱虫携带的疾病。他接种了莱姆病疫苗，并每月服用一片裹着喷雾奶酪的咀嚼片，以防跳蚤、蜱虫和心丝虫——一种通过蚊子叮咬传播的疾病。目前有几种针对狗和猫的防蜱治疗方法，通常依赖能够在蜱虫叮咬后将其杀死的化学物质。

它们便开始进食。通常，这些药物要么直接涂抹在皮肤上作为“滴剂”，要么通过项圈散发，要么以药片形式服用。然而，为人类开发预防性药物并非易事。人体研究比动物研究更困难且成本更高。在人体试验中，科学家通常需要招募大量参与者，并在他们日常生活中长期跟踪。这是因为只有一小部分人会被叮咬并感染蜱传疾病，而必须有足够多的感染病例才能证明疫苗或药物是否有效。与此同时，在动物试验中，研究人员常常直接将感染蜱放在动物身上，几乎确保它们会感染特定蜱传病原体，从而使试验更容易进行。但科学家对在人体中开展莱姆病的所谓“挑战试验”犹豫不决，部分原因是他们不想冒险让参与者出现长期持续的症状。马萨诸塞州塔夫茨大学医学院免疫学教授林登·胡表示：“我认为没人会报名参加莱姆病试验。”他曾与多家公司合作研究针对人类的抗蜱策略。他解释说，这正是此类试验难以获批的原因。然而，1998年美国曾批准过一种人类莱姆病疫苗，名为LYMErix。该疫苗在超过1万名参与者中进行了试验，预防疾病的有效性达76%。但市场需求低迷，部分原因是关于副作用（即关节炎）的报告和诉讼。2002年，卫生官员审查了数据，未发现安全风险证据。尽管如此，该疫苗的制造商同年以需求不足为由停产。如今，蜱传疾病风险人群日益增多，激发了预防领域的新投资。特别是，寻找另一种莱姆病疫苗的进程正在加快——并开始初见成效。目前进展最快的候选疫苗是辉瑞和瓦尔内瓦公司开发的PF-07307405。它与旧版LYMErix疫苗及为犬类设计的疫苗具有相似靶点——即莱姆病致病菌伯氏疏螺旋体表面的一种名为OspA的蛋白质片段。该疫苗促使人体免疫系统产生针对美国和欧洲常见的六种OspA变体的抗体。当感染蜱叮咬人体并吸血时，它也会摄入人体抗体。在蜱体内，抗体会附着在OspA上，阻止细菌离开蜱虫。“你的抗体能在细菌仍处于蜱体内时将其消灭，从而从一开始就防止感染，”哈特说。今年早些时候，辉瑞宣布重新

一项三期试验的结果显示，四剂次方案在预防莱姆病方面的有效性超过70%，该试验涉及9400多人，旨在测试新干预措施与现有疗法或安慰剂的对比效果及其安全性。然而，试验期间患莱姆病的参与者少于预期，这意味着结果不如研究团队所希望的那样确凿。未发现重大安全隐患，辉瑞在新闻稿中表示，对其疫苗潜力充满信心，并计划提交给美国政府监管机构审批。纽约康奈尔大学兽医学院助理教授、新兴传染病研究员劳拉·古德曼表示：“一旦上市，我肯定会立即接种。”同样，莫德纳正在测试两种针对OspA蛋白的莱姆病疫苗，两者均处于二期试验阶段，该阶段在比一期更大的人群中测试干预措施，以评估其安全性和有效性。与此同时，耶鲁大学的研究人员正在研究一种促使免疫系统对蜱虫唾液产生反应的注射剂，该注射剂尚未进行人体试验。

另一种选择是完全跳过疫苗。马萨诸塞大学陈医学院医学教授马克·克莱姆普纳十多年来一直在开发一种针对OspA蛋白的注射剂。疫苗通过触发免疫系统产生抗体来起作用，而这种注射剂则直接将预制抗体输送到人体内，仅需两天即可吸收足够抗体，提供四个月的保护。莱姆病并非在所有有蜱虫的地方都存在，例如在美国东南部就很少感染，那里的蜱虫更喜欢叮咬蜥蜴而非哺乳动物。克莱姆普纳表示，这种注射剂的设计理念是，生活在莱姆病流行地区或在该地区工作、旅行的人可以在蜱虫季节开始时接种，之后再接种第二剂。该产品名为TNX-4800，已通过一期临床试验，该阶段旨在确定安全剂量并识别潜在副作用。Tonix制药公司于2025年获得其许可，据公司网站称，计划明年启动二期临床试验。更多相关内容：• 科学家如何逼近病毒的“弱点” • 对HIV免疫的罕见人群 • 为什么蚊子更爱叮咬某些人？另一家制药公司Tarsus制药正在研发一种药丸，采用与狗用抗蜱药物相同的成分。该药物TP-05干扰蜱虫的神经系统并迅速杀死它们，希望能在蜱虫有机会传播疾病之前发挥作用。

##段落
nsmit莱姆病致病菌及其他病原体。在犬类中，该药物以咀嚼片形式存在，但在人类中将以药丸形式使用。今年3月，Tarsus公司宣布已启动人体二期临床试验，结果预计将于明年上半年公布。

##段落
“我认为这将改变游戏规则，”康涅狄格州耶鲁大学公共卫生学院流行病学名誉教授Durland Fish表示，他数十年研究包括莱姆病在内的媒介传播疾病。他说，这种药丸还可能预防其他日益增多的蜱传疾病，包括巴贝斯虫病和无形体病。但目前尚不清楚这些选项何时以及是否会投入使用。

##段落
与此同时，最佳预防措施仍是首先防止蜱虫叮咬。这意味着远离高草丛、穿着防护衣物，并在进屋后淋浴和检查是否有蜱虫。这些久经考验的方法确实有效，Hu说，但人们可能难以坚持。“人们会感到疲惫或深夜在外，孩子们也会烦躁不安，”Hu说。他表示，这正是疫苗或药丸能发挥作用的地方——人们服用后无需每次出门都记得采取措施——这可能“真正带来公共卫生益处”。

readings.title: Feeling unseen by your boss? Here’s what you can do
body: Feeling unseen by your boss? Here’s what you can do

Ever have your hard work — including your successes — go unnoticed by your manager? Fixable , TED’s new podcast, is here to do just that — to fix the problems of everyday people who call in with their work woes.

In episode four , cohosts and top leadership coaches Frances Frei and Anne Morriss got to know Nai’a, a caller who struggled with receiving recognition after a major reorganization paired her with a new and preoccupied boss. Nai’a was going above and beyond to do her job well, but the lack of acknowledgement and encouragement — and even awareness — of her work was causing her to lose motivation.
Frances’s and Anne’s first piece of advice to Nai’a was simple: See the humanness of what’s going on — and of your manager.

“Sometimes the barrier to showing up as a great collaborator with your manager can be that there’s still some residual frustration about the situation,” Anne explained. “But that emotion is not going to be useful to you.”
Instead, they encouraged Nai’a to recognize the humanity of her manager and forgive them for making mistakes.
Frances and Anne also shared this strategy with her to practice: Choose curiosity over judgment.

Here’s how Frances put it: “You have a choice between judgment and curiosity, because both can’t exist at the same time. So if you have judgment about your manager, you can’t really be curious about their situation. And when you’re thinking of your manager as a person who’s got a lot of part-time jobs, how do we set them up for success?”

“The simplest expression of curiosity — which is truly a magical elixir in a workplace — is in the form of questions,” said Anne. For example, you could start by asking your manager what process works best for them to learn about your accomplishments and contributions. Or, you could focus on how you can make your meetings with them more productive by asking them, “How can our one-on-one time be of service to what we’re trying to achieve together?”

Another option: Be open about your concerns, and ask your manager what their vision of your success looks like. You could say something like, “Here’s my fear: I’m working really hard, and in this state of flux, I’m afraid that six months will go by and people are going to wonder whether or not I did a good job. So it’s just helpful for me to be clear — what is a good job and how can I help in getting that data for you?”

Across industries and across the world, many people are going through workplace reorganizations and other sweeping changes. And like Nai’a, it’s normal to feel anxious and stressed by what’s happening and to need to go through a readjustment period. Leading with questions — and seeing your boss as another human you’re collaborating with — can help you gain back some agency and autonomy.

“Try doing what you can, and marvel at how the other person changes as a result, as opposed to coming up with the list of how you would like the other person to change,” said Frances. “I think you’re going to be pleasantly surprised; that’s the beautiful part of this.”

No matter your job or business, you’ll find actionable advice on Fixable that can improve your workdays. In other episodes, learn how to overcome communication roadblocks, scale up your side project and lead more productive meetings. Plus: Click here for a chance to get your own work question answered on the show! Listen to Fixable now wherever you get your podcasts.
About the author Hayley Caldwell is a copywriter on the Audience Development team at TED.

你是否曾有过这样的经历：你的努力工作——包括你的成功——被经理忽视？TED的新播客《Fixable》正是为此而来——解决那些带着工作烦恼打来电话的普通人的问题。  
在第四集中，联合主持人兼顶级领导力教练弗朗西丝·弗雷和安妮·莫里斯认识了来电者奈阿，她在一次重大重组后，被分配了一位忙碌且心不在焉的老板，因此难以获得认可。奈阿尽心尽力想把工作做好，但缺乏肯定、鼓励——甚至是对她工作的关注——导致她逐渐失去动力。  
弗朗西丝和安妮给奈阿的第一条建议很简单：看清事情中的人性——以及你经理的人性。  
“有时，作为优秀合作者与经理相处的障碍，可能源于你对现状仍残留的些许挫败感，”安妮解释道。“但那种情绪对你不会有帮助。”  
相反，她们鼓励奈阿去体察经理的人性，并原谅他们犯错。  
弗朗西丝和安妮还分享了这一策略供她实践：选择好奇，而非评判。  
弗朗西丝是这样说的：“你可以在评判和好奇之间做选择，因为两者无法同时存在。所以，如果你对经理有评判，你就无法真正对他们的处境感到好奇。而当你把经理看作一个身兼数职的人时，我们该如何帮助他们成功？”  
“好奇心的最简单表达——在工作场所中堪称神奇灵药——就是提问的形式，”安妮说。例如，你可以先问经理，了解你的成就和贡献的最佳方式是什么。或者，你可以专注于如何让与他们的会议更高效，比如问：“我们的一对一时间如何能服务于我们共同追求的目标？”  
另一个选择：坦诚你的担忧，并询问经理他们对你成功的愿景是什么。你可以这样说：“我的担忧是：我工作非常努力，在这种变动状态下，我担心六个月过去后，人们会怀疑我是否做好本职工作。所以，对我而言，明确什么是‘做得好’以及我如何帮你获取相关数据，会很有帮助。”  
在各行各业和世界各地，许多人正在经历职场重组和其他大规模变革。和奈阿一样，对正在发生的事情感到焦虑和压力，并需要经历一段调整期，这都是正常的。

##段落
带着问题去沟通——并且把老板视为与你协作的另一个人——能帮你重新获得一些主动权和自主性。

##段落
“试着做你能做的，然后观察对方因此发生的变化，而不是列出一张你希望对方如何改变的清单，”弗朗西斯说。“我认为你会惊喜地发现，这正是这件事的美妙之处。”

##段落
无论你从事什么工作或经营什么业务，你都能在《Fixable》节目中找到改善工作日的实用建议。在其他集数中，学习如何克服沟通障碍、扩展你的副业项目，以及主持更高效的会议。另外：点击这里，有机会在节目中提出你自己的职场问题并获得解答！现在就在你获取播客的任何平台收听《Fixable》。

dialogs.title: At the check-in counter
dialogs.goal: 练习护照/行李/座位相关表达，从容应对值机

lines.en: Good morning. May I see your passport and booking reference, please?
lines.zh: 早上好，请出示您的护照和预订编号。

lines.en: Sure, here you are. I'd like a window seat if possible.
lines.zh: 好的，给您。如果可以的话我想要靠窗的座位。

lines.en: I can arrange that. Are you checking in any bags today?
lines.zh: 可以安排。您今天有要托运的行李吗？

lines.en: Just one suitcase. Does it meet the weight limit?
lines.zh: 就一个行李箱。它超重了吗？

lines.en: It's within the limit. Your boarding pass is ready — gate 22, boarding at 10:40.
lines.zh: 在限额内。您的登机牌好了——22 号登机口，10:40 登机。

lines.en: Great. Could you also confirm that my carry-on bag fits the cabin size requirements?
lines.zh: 太好了。您能再确认一下我的随身行李符合客舱尺寸要求吗？

lines.en: Let me check the dimensions. Yes, it fits within our standard allowance. You're all set for the cabin.
lines.zh: 让我看一下尺寸。是的，符合我们的标准限额。您的客舱行李没问题。

lines.en: Perfect. By the way, is there any chance I could get an aisle seat instead? I just realized I may need to stretch my legs.
lines.zh: 太好了。顺便问一下，我能改成过道座位吗？我刚意识到可能需要伸伸腿。

lines.en: Certainly. Let me update that for you — I've moved you to 21C, an aisle seat. No problem at all.
lines.zh: 当然可以。我来为您更新——已为您调到21C，过道座位。完全没问题。

lines.en: Thank you so much. One last thing — what time should I be at the gate?
lines.zh: 非常感谢。最后问一下，我应该在什么时间到登机口？

lines.en: Please be at the gate at least 30 minutes before boarding. Enjoy your flight, and have a wonderful trip!
lines.zh: 请在登机前至少30分钟到达登机口。祝您飞行愉快，旅途顺利！

dialogs.title: Small talk at a conference
dialogs.goal: 用自然的破冰句开启商务对话，并过渡到合作话题

lines.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Echo, from the consumer insights team.
lines.zh: 你好，我们好像还没见过。我是 Echo，来自消费者洞察团队。

lines.en: Nice to meet you. I work on product strategy. What brings you to this session?
lines.zh: 很高兴认识你。我做产品策略。你为什么来听这场？

lines.en: I'm exploring how AI is changing our research methods. Have you seen anything useful today?
lines.zh: 我在研究 AI 如何改变我们的研究方法。你今天有看到什么有用的吗？

lines.en: Actually, yes — a talk on real-time consumer signals. We should compare notes sometime.
lines.zh: 其实有——一个关于实时消费者信号的演讲。我们应该找个时间交流一下。

lines.en: I'd love that. Let's grab coffee after the keynote.
lines.zh: 太好了。主题演讲后我们喝杯咖啡吧。

lines.en: Sounds good. By the way, how does your team currently handle qualitative data?
lines.zh: 听起来不错。顺便问一下，你们团队目前是怎么处理定性数据的？

lines.en: We still rely heavily on manual coding, which is time-consuming. That's why I'm keen on AI-driven tools.
lines.zh: 我们还是主要靠人工编码，很耗时。所以我对 AI 驱动的工具很感兴趣。

lines.en: Interesting. We've been piloting a sentiment analysis model that might complement your workflow.
lines.zh: 有意思。我们一直在试点一个情绪分析模型，可能和你们的工作流互补。

lines.en: That sounds promising. Could you share a bit more about how it handles multilingual data?
lines.zh: 听起来很有前景。你能多分享一下它如何处理多语言数据吗？

lines.en: Sure — it's trained on several major languages, but accuracy varies. Maybe we can set up a quick demo next week.
lines.zh: 当然——它在几种主要语言上训练过，但准确率有差异。也许我们下周可以安排一个快速演示。

lines.en: Perfect. I'll bring our research lead along. Let's exchange contacts and follow up by email.
lines.zh: 完美。我会带上我们的研究负责人。我们交换一下联系方式，然后邮件跟进吧。

dialogs.title: Checking into a hotel
dialogs.goal: 掌握入住登记、特殊需求与Wi-Fi等常用句

lines.en: Good evening. Do you have a reservation under the name Lee?
lines.zh: 晚上好。请问有预订在 Lee 名下吗？

lines.en: Yes, for two nights. Is breakfast included?
lines.zh: 有的，住两晚。含早餐吗？

lines.en: It is — served from 7 to 10. Could I have a room on a higher floor, away from the elevator?
lines.zh: 含的——7 点到 10 点供应。可以安排高一点、远离电梯的房间吗？

lines.en: Certainly. Here's your key card, and the Wi-Fi password is on this slip.
lines.zh: 当然可以。这是您的房卡，Wi-Fi 密码在这张纸上。

lines.en: Thank you. Could you also confirm the checkout time for me?
lines.zh: 谢谢。另外能帮我确认一下退房时间吗？

lines.en: Checkout is at noon, but we offer a late checkout until 2 PM for an additional fee.
lines.zh: 退房时间是中午12点，不过我们可以提供延迟至下午2点的退房服务，需额外收费。

lines.en: That's good to know. I might take advantage of that. Is there a gym or pool on site?
lines.zh: 这信息很有用，我可能会用到。酒店内有健身房或游泳池吗？

lines.en: Yes, both are on the second floor, open from 6 AM to 10 PM. Towels are provided at the front desk.
lines.zh: 有的，两者都在二楼，开放时间为早上6点到晚上10点。毛巾可在前台领取。

lines.en: Perfect. One more thing — could you arrange a wake-up call at 7:30 tomorrow morning?
lines.zh: 太好了。还有一件事——能帮我安排明早7:30的叫醒服务吗？

lines.en: Of course. I've noted that for room 1208. Is there anything else you need?
lines.zh: 当然可以。我已为您记录在1208房间。还有其他需要吗？

lines.en: No, that's all for now. Thanks for your help.
lines.zh: 暂时没有了，谢谢你的帮助。

dialogs.title: Ordering with dietary needs
dialogs.goal: 清晰表达过敏/忌口，避免误会

lines.en: Welcome! Have you decided what you'd like to order?
lines.zh: 欢迎！您决定好点什么了吗？

lines.en: Not yet. I'm allergic to peanuts — could you tell me which dishes are safe?
lines.zh: 还没。我对花生过敏——能告诉我哪些菜是安全的吗？

lines.en: Of course. The grilled fish and the vegetable soup are both nut-free. I'll note the allergy for the kitchen.
lines.zh: 当然。烤鱼和蔬菜汤都不含坚果。我会在厨房单上标注过敏。

lines.en: Perfect, thank you. Could I also get that without spicy sauce?
lines.zh: 太好了，谢谢。那份可以不放辣酱吗？

lines.en: Absolutely. I'll make sure the chef prepares it with a mild seasoning instead. Would you like any appetizer to start?
lines.zh: 完全可以。我会确保厨师改用清淡调味。需要先来点开胃菜吗？

lines.en: Yes, the spring rolls look good — but are they fried in peanut oil?
lines.zh: 好的，春卷看起来不错——但那是用花生油炸的吗？

lines.en: Good question. We use canola oil for frying, so they're safe. However, the dipping sauce contains sesame paste — would you like it on the side?
lines.zh: 问得好。我们用菜籽油炸，所以是安全的。不过蘸酱含芝麻酱——需要单独放旁边吗？

lines.en: That would be great. Please keep the sauce separate, and I'll decide whether to use it.
lines.zh: 那太好了。请把酱单独放，我自己决定要不要用。

lines.en: Understood. I'll also check with the kitchen on the dessert options — the mango pudding is peanut-free, but the chocolate cake may contain traces.
lines.zh: 明白了。我还会和厨房确认甜点选项——芒果布丁不含花生，但巧克力蛋糕可能含微量。

lines.en: Thanks for being so thorough. I'll go with the mango pudding then.
lines.zh: 谢谢你这么仔细。那我就选芒果布丁吧。

lines.en: Great choice. I'll place your order now and confirm everything with the chef. Your safety is our priority.
lines.zh: 好选择。我现在下单并和厨师确认所有细节。您的安全是我们的首要任务。

dialogs.title: Talking about AI at work
dialogs.goal: 用职场商务英语表达对 AI 的看法与担忧

lines.en: Have you tried the new AI assistant? It's been a game-changer for my drafts.
lines.zh: 你试过新的 AI 助手了吗？它彻底改变了我写草稿的方式。

lines.en: I have, but I'm cautious. I double-check everything it produces.
lines.zh: 试过，但我比较谨慎。它生成的东西我都会复核。

lines.en: Fair enough. I see it as a starting point, not the final answer.
lines.zh: 有道理。我把它当作起点，而不是最终答案。

lines.en: Exactly. The human touch still matters most with our clients.
lines.zh: 没错。对咱们的客户来说，人情味依然最重要。

lines.en: That said, I've noticed it saves me at least two hours a day on research and summarization.
lines.zh: 话虽如此，我注意到它每天至少帮我在研究和总结上省下两个小时。

lines.en: I can see that. But what about accuracy? I've caught it making subtle errors in data interpretation.
lines.zh: 这我能理解。但准确性呢？我抓到过它在数据解读上犯一些很细微的错误。

lines.en: I've seen that too. That's why I always cross-reference its output with our internal reports.
lines.zh: 我也遇到过。所以我才总是拿它生成的内容和咱们内部报告做交叉核对。

lines.en: Good practice. My concern is more about long-term dependency—are we losing our own analytical skills?
lines.zh: 好习惯。我更担心的是长期依赖——我们会不会失去自己的分析能力？

lines.en: That's a valid point. I try to use it as a tool, not a crutch. I still do the critical thinking myself.
lines.zh: 这点提得很对。我尽量把它当工具，而不是拐杖。关键思考还是我自己来。

lines.en: I think we need a team guideline on when and how to use AI, especially for client-facing documents.
lines.zh: 我觉得咱们需要一份团队指南，明确什么时候、怎么用 AI，尤其是面对客户的文档。

lines.en: Agreed. Let's bring that up in next week's meeting—maybe we can draft a policy together.
lines.zh: 同意。咱们下周会上提一下——也许可以一起起草一份规范。

dialogs.title: Briefing a Descriptive Panel
dialogs.zhTitle: 为描述性感官评价小组做导入简报
dialogs.goal: 掌握主持感官评价小组时的标准指令语言与"去引导化"表达。

lines.en: Good morning, everyone. Before we start, a quick reminder: we are not looking for whether you like the sample. We are looking for what you perceive.
lines.zh: 早上好。开始之前提醒一下：我们不是要知道你喜不喜欢这个样品，而是要知道你感知到了什么。

lines.en: So we should keep preference out of it entirely?
lines.zh: 所以我们要完全把偏好排除在外？

lines.en: Exactly. Intensity, not preference. If something is very sweet and you personally hate it, the score is still high.
lines.zh: 正是。评的是强度，不是喜好。如果某样东西很甜而你个人讨厌它，分数依然要打高。

lines.en: Understood. And the order of the samples?
lines.zh: 明白了。样品顺序呢？

lines.en: Balanced and randomised, as always. Please cleanse your palate with water and the unsalted cracker between each one, and wait ninety seconds.
lines.zh: 照例是平衡随机化的。每个样品之间请用清水和无盐饼干清口，并等待 90 秒。

lines.en: What if I pick up an attribute that is not on the ballot?
lines.zh: 如果我感知到一个评分表上没有的属性怎么办？

lines.en: Write it in the open field. Honestly, those are often the most useful lines on the whole sheet.
lines.zh: 写在开放栏里。说实话，那些往往是整张表上最有价值的内容。

lines.en: Should I try to match the vocabulary we agreed on in training?
lines.zh: 我需要尽量用我们培训时统一的词汇吗？

lines.en: Use the lexicon where it fits, but do not force it. A forced term hides more than it reveals.
lines.zh: 合适的地方就用词典里的术语，但别硬套。硬套的术语掩盖的比揭示的多。

lines.en: One last thing — no discussion during evaluation. We compare notes only in the debrief.
lines.zh: 最后一点——评价过程中不要交流。我们只在总结环节比对结果。

keys.zh: 评强度，不评偏好（感官分析第一原则）
平衡随机化（样品呈送设计）

dialogs.title: Presenting Findings the Client Did Not Want
dialogs.zhTitle: 汇报一个客户不想听到的结论
dialogs.goal: 练习在坏消息中保持专业与建设性的商务表达。

lines.en: So, bottom line — does the new formulation win?
lines.zh: 所以，直接说结论——新配方赢了吗？

lines.en: Not on the measure you asked about. But I would argue you were asking about the wrong measure.
lines.zh: 在你问的那个指标上没有。但我认为，你问的可能不是该问的那个指标。

lines.en: Go on.
lines.zh: 你说。

lines.en: Overall liking is flat — statistically indistinguishable. However, the new formulation scores significantly higher on perceived care and product quality cues.
lines.zh: 总体喜好度持平，统计上无差异。但新配方在"感知到的用心程度"和"品质线索"上显著更高。

lines.en: Does that translate into anything commercial?
lines.zh: 这能转化成商业结果吗？

lines.en: It correlates strongly with repurchase intent in this category. Liking predicts the first purchase; quality cues predict the fourth.
lines.zh: 在这个品类里，它与复购意向高度相关。喜好度预测第一次购买，品质线索预测第四次。

lines.en: That is a bolder claim than I expected from you.
lines.zh: 这比我预期的你会说的话要大胆。

lines.en: It is in the appendix with the regression. I would rather show you the uncomfortable version now than the comfortable one in six months.
lines.zh: 附录里有回归结果。我宁愿现在给你看那个不舒服的版本，也不想六个月后给你看那个舒服的版本。

lines.en: Fair. What would you do if this were your decision?
lines.zh: 有道理。如果是你来定，你会怎么做？

lines.en: Ship it, but rewrite the claim. You are selling reassurance, not novelty.
lines.zh: 上市，但改掉宣称。你卖的是安心感，不是新奇感。

dialogs.title: A Tight Connection
dialogs.goal: 掌握机场改签、行李与登机口相关的高频表达。

lines.en: Excuse me, my inbound flight was delayed and I have fifty minutes to make my connection. Will I be all right?
lines.zh: 打扰一下，我来程航班延误了，中转只剩 50 分钟。来得及吗？

lines.en: It is tight but doable. Are you checked through to your final destination?
lines.zh: 有点紧但可以。您的行李是直挂到终点的吗？

lines.en: Yes, my luggage is tagged all the way through. Do I need to clear security again?
lines.zh: 是的，行李直挂到底。我需要重新过安检吗？

lines.en: You will, at the transfer point. Follow the purple signs, and mention your connection time at the desk — they can fast-track you.
lines.zh: 需要，在中转处。跟着紫色指示牌走，在柜台说明您的中转时间，他们可以帮您走快速通道。

lines.en: That is a relief. And if I miss it, what are my options?
lines.zh: 那我就放心了。万一没赶上，我有什么选择？

lines.en: You would be rebooked on the next available flight at no charge, since the delay was ours.
lines.zh: 因为延误是我们造成的，您会被免费改签到下一个有位的航班。

lines.en: Could you note my seat preference now, just in case? Aisle, towards the front.
lines.zh: 能不能现在先记下我的座位偏好，以防万一？靠走道，靠前一点。

lines.en: Noted. Here is your boarding pass. Gate B22 — boarding closes twenty minutes before departure.
lines.zh: 记下了。这是您的登机牌。B22 登机口，起飞前 20 分钟停止登机。

lines.en: Thank you. One more thing — is there anywhere to grab a quick coffee on the way?
lines.zh: 谢谢。还有一件事——路上有地方能快速买杯咖啡吗？

lines.en: There is a kiosk right past security. Honestly, with fifty minutes, I would skip it.
lines.zh: 过了安检就有个小店。不过说实话，只有 50 分钟的话，我建议您别去了。

dialogs.title: Explaining What You Do at a Dinner Party
dialogs.zhTitle: 在饭局上解释你到底是做什么的
dialogs.goal: 练习用非专业语言介绍专业工作，这是最难也最有用的能力。

lines.en: So what do you actually do? Something with market research?
lines.zh: 你到底是做什么的？跟市场调研有关？

lines.en: Sort of. I work on how products feel — taste, texture, smell — and why people prefer one over another.
lines.zh: 算是吧。我研究产品给人的感受——味道、质地、气味——以及人们为什么更偏爱其中一个。

lines.en: Wait, that is a real job? Who pays for that?
lines.zh: 等等，这是个真实存在的职业？谁会为这个付钱？

lines.en: Anyone who makes something you put in your mouth or on your skin. If two products cost the same, the one that feels right wins.
lines.zh: 任何做入口或上脸产品的公司。两个产品价格一样，感觉对的那个就赢了。

lines.en: Give me an example.
lines.zh: 举个例子。

lines.en: Sure. Think about the sound a jar makes when you first open it. That pop is engineered, and it makes the food taste fresher.
lines.zh: 好。想想第一次拧开一个罐子时的声音。那声"啵"是设计出来的，它会让食物尝起来更新鲜。

lines.en: You are telling me I have been manipulated by a lid.
lines.zh: 你是说我一直在被一个盖子操纵。

lines.en: I would say informed by a lid. Your brain uses every clue it can get, and sound is a very cheap clue.
lines.zh: 我会说是被一个盖子"告知"了。你的大脑会用上一切能拿到的线索，而声音是最廉价的一种。

lines.en: Does knowing all this ruin it for you?
lines.zh: 知道这些会不会让你失去乐趣？

lines.en: Occasionally. But mostly it does the opposite — it turns an ordinary Tuesday breakfast into something worth paying attention to.
lines.zh: 偶尔会。但大多数时候是反过来的——它让一个普通周二的早餐变成值得留意的东西。

keys.en: the one that feels right wins

keys.zh: 被操纵 / 被告知（一组有分寸感的对比）

dialogs.title: Pushing Back on an Impossible Timeline
dialogs.zhTitle: 拒绝一个不可能的排期
dialogs.goal: 练习职场中"有边界感但不对抗"的英文表达。

lines.en: We need the consumer test results by the fifteenth. Can you make that work?
lines.zh: 我们需要在 15 号前拿到消费者测试结果。你能做到吗？

lines.en: Let me walk you through what fifteenth would require, and then you can decide.
lines.zh: 我先带你过一遍 15 号意味着什么，然后你来决定。

lines.en: Okay.
lines.zh: 好。

lines.en: Recruitment alone is eight working days for this profile. That leaves two days for fieldwork and one for analysis.
lines.zh: 光是招募��类人群就要 8 个工作日。剩下 2 天做执行，1 天做分析。

lines.en: Could we shorten recruitment?
lines.zh: 招募能压缩吗？

lines.en: We could, but then we take whoever is available, and 'whoever is available' is a real bias, not a rounding error.
lines.zh: 可以，但那样我们只能要"谁有空要谁"，而"谁有空"是一个真实的偏差，不是舍入误差。

lines.en: What would you propose?
lines.zh: 你的建议是？

lines.en: Two options. A directional read on the fifteenth with a clear health warning, or a defensible result on the twenty-second.
lines.zh: 两个选项。15 号给一个方向性判断，并附明确的局限说明；或者 22 号给一个经得起挑战的结论。

lines.en: The steering committee meets on the eighteenth.
lines.zh: 指导委员会 18 号开会。

lines.en: Then take the directional read, and let me write the caveat slide myself. If someone quotes it out of context in a board deck, we both pay for it.
lines.zh: 那就用方向性判断，但局限说明那页让我自己写。如果有人把它断章取义放进董事会材料，我们两个都要付代价。

lines.en: Deal.
lines.zh: 成交。

keys.zh: 方向性判断（非定论性结论）
不是可以忽略的小误差

dialogs.title: A Room With a Problem
dialogs.goal: 练习礼貌而坚定的投诉与协商。

lines.en: Hi, I checked in about an hour ago into 704. I am afraid the room is not going to work.
lines.zh: 你好，我大约一小时前入住 704。恐怕这个房间不太行。

lines.en: I am sorry to hear that. May I ask what the issue is?
lines.zh: 很抱歉。方便问一下是什么问题吗？

lines.en: There is a persistent smell of damp, and the air conditioning is quite loud. I have an early start tomorrow.
lines.zh: 有一股持续的潮味，空调也挺吵。我明天要早起。

lines.en: Let me see what else we have. We are fairly full tonight.
lines.zh: 我看看还有什么房。今晚我们几乎满房。

lines.en: I appreciate that. I am not asking for an upgrade — just somewhere quiet and dry.
lines.zh: 我理解。我不是要求升级——只想要一个安静干燥的房间。

lines.en: I can offer you 1102. It is a similar layout, higher floor, away from the lift shaft.
lines.zh: 我可以给您 1102。户型相近，楼层更高，远离电梯井。

lines.en: That sounds much better. Could someone help me move the bags?
lines.zh: 那好多了。能安排人帮我搬一下行李吗？

lines.en: Of course. And I will note a late checkout on your booking for the inconvenience.
lines.zh: 当然。另外我会在您的订单上备注延迟退房，作为对不便的补偿。

lines.en: That is very kind — thank you for sorting it out so quickly.
lines.zh: 太贴心了——谢谢你这么快就处理好。

lines.en: You are most welcome. I will have the bellman bring up your new key shortly.
lines.zh: 不客气。我会让行李员马上把新房卡送上去。

lines.en: Perfect. I will head up now and get settled. Thanks again for your help.
lines.zh: 太好了。我现在就上去安顿。再次感谢你的帮助。

keys.en: I am not asking for an upgrade
keys.zh: 我并不是要求升级（降低对抗感）

dialogs.title: Small Talk at a Conference Coffee Break
dialogs.zhTitle: 会议茶歇上的专业闲聊
dialogs.goal: 练习从寒暄自然过渡到有价值的专业交流。

lines.en: That last session was a bit of a sales pitch, was it not?
lines.zh: 刚那场基本就是个推销吧？

lines.en: A little. Though the bit about implicit measurement was worth staying for.
lines.zh: 有一点。不过关于内隐测量的那一段还是值得留下来听的。

lines.en: Are you on the client side or agency?
lines.zh: 你是甲方还是乙方？

lines.en: Client side — I look after sensory and consumer insights for a personal care portfolio.
lines.zh: 甲方——我负责一个个护品类组合的感官与消费者洞察。

lines.en: Then you must be dealing with the AI question constantly.
lines.zh: 那你肯定天天在面对 AI 那个问题。

lines.en: Constantly. My working position is that AI is excellent before fieldwork and dangerous after it.
lines.zh: 天天。我目前的立场是：AI 在田野之前很好用，在田野之后很危险。

lines.en: That is a neat way of putting it. Where do you draw the line exactly?
lines.zh: 这个说法很精炼。你具体在哪里划这条线？

lines.en: Anything that generates hypotheses, yes. Anything that generates respondents, no.
lines.zh: 任何用来生成假设的，可以。任何用来生成受访者的，不行。

lines.en: I might steal that for my next steering group.
lines.zh: 我下次开指导会可能要借用一下这句。

lines.en: Please do. Are you around for the afternoon panel? I would be curious what you make of it.
lines.zh: 尽管用。你下午的圆桌还在吗？我挺想听听你怎么看。

keys.en: a bit of a sales pitch
where do you draw the line

dialogs.title: Moderating a Focus Group
dialogs.zhTitle: 主持一场焦点小组访谈
dialogs.goal: 练习在焦点小组中保持中立、追问而不引导、妥善处理冷场与分歧。

lines.en: Let's start simple — when you first tasted this, what was the very first thing that came to mind?
lines.zh: 咱们从简单处开始——你第一口尝到时，最先冒出来的念头是什么？

lines.en: It felt… clean? Like, not heavy on the tongue.
lines.zh: 感觉……很干净？就是说，舌头上不厚重。

lines.en: Clean — can you stay with that word for a second? What makes it feel clean versus, say, watery?
lines.zh: “干净”——你能就这个词再多说一点吗？它和所谓“寡淡”的区别在哪？

lines.en: For me clean means no aftertaste. Watery would be thin and forgettable.
lines.zh: 对我来说干净就是没有余味。寡淡则是单薄、喝完就忘了。

lines.en: Good distinction. Anyone feel something different in the aftertaste?
lines.zh: 这个区分很好。有人对余味有不同感受吗？

lines.en: There's a slight bitterness at the end. Not bad, just… present.
lines.zh: 尾段有一点苦。不讨厌，就是……存在感。

lines.en: Noted — a late bitterness. And does that bitterness make you want to take another sip, or stop?
lines.zh: 记下了——尾段苦。这种苦是让你想再喝一口，还是想停下？

lines.en: Actually it makes me curious. I'd go again.
lines.zh: 其实它让我有点好奇。我会再喝。

lines.en: Curious is interesting. So the bitterness isn't a reject signal here?
lines.zh: “好奇”这个点有意思。所以这里的苦并不是拒绝信号？

lines.en: No, it feels intentional. Like the product knows what it's doing.
lines.zh: 不是，它感觉是刻意的。像产品心里有数。

keys.en: first thing that came to mind

dialogs.title: Ordering at a Café
dialogs.goal: 掌握点单、定制规格、堂食外带与确认等待时间的日常高频表达。

lines.en: Hi! What can I get for you?
lines.zh: 您好！要点点什么？

lines.en: Could I get a medium flat white, please? With oat milk if you have it.
lines.zh: 麻烦来一杯中杯澳白，可以的话用燕麦奶。

lines.en: Sure — oat milk, medium flat white. Anything to eat?
lines.zh: 好的——燕麦奶，中杯澳白。要配点吃的吗？

lines.en: Maybe one of those almond croissants. Is it still warm?
lines.zh: 来一个那个杏仁可颂吧。现在还是热的吗？

lines.en: Just came out of the oven. Want it heated a little more?
lines.zh: 刚出炉。要再加热一下吗？

lines.en: That'd be great, thank you. And could I get that to stay, not takeaway?
lines.zh: 那太好了，谢谢。这杯我要堂食，不要外带。

lines.en: For here. Name for the cup?
lines.zh: 堂食。杯子写什么名字？

lines.en: It's Echo. How long should I expect to wait?
lines.zh: 写 Echo。大概要等多久？

lines.en: About four minutes — I'll bring it over to your table.
lines.zh: 大概四分钟——我给你送到座位上。

lines.en: Perfect, thanks so much.
lines.zh: 太好了，非常感谢。

dialogs.title: Negotiating a Specification With a Supplier
dialogs.zhTitle: 与供应商谈一份感官规格
dialogs.goal: 练习就感官规格、批次公差与交付节奏与供应商沟通，守住品质底线。

lines.en: So you want the sweetness capped at level 3 on your scale?
lines.zh: 所以你们希望甜度上限压在你们量表的 3 级？

lines.en: Level 3, and critically — no more than a half-step variance between batches.
lines.zh: 3 级，而且关键是——批次之间波动不能超过半级。

lines.en: Half a step is tight. That means we re-calibrate the line every run.
lines.zh: 半级很紧。那意味着每批我们都要重新校准产线。

lines.en: I understand the cost. But the consumer test showed anything above 3.5 drops purchase intent.
lines.zh: 成本我理解。但消费者测试显示，超过 3.5 购买意向就掉。

lines.en: Fair. What if we hold 3.0 to 3.3 and flag anything outside?
lines.zh: 合理。那我们控制在 3.0 到 3.3，超出的做标记，行吗？

lines.en: That works, as long as the flag triggers a hold, not a shipment.
lines.zh: 可以，前提是标记触发的是“扣留”，不是“发货”。

lines.en: Agreed — out-of-band goes to quarantine, not the truck.
lines.zh: 同意——超范围的进待检区，不上车。

lines.en: And lead time? We can't promise the same volume if batches fail.
lines.zh: 那交期呢？如果批次出问题，我们给不了同样产量。

lines.en: We'll build in a 10% buffer stock. You get first refusal on it.
lines.zh: 我们会留 10% 缓冲库存。你们有优先调配权。

lines.en: Good. Let's put the tolerance in writing before pilot.
lines.zh: 好。试点前我们把公差写进合同。

dialogs.title: Getting Directions on the Street
dialogs.goal: 掌握问路、确认距离、交通方式切换与表达感谢的实用句型。

lines.en: Excuse me, is the metro station far from here?
lines.zh: 打扰一下，地铁站离这儿远吗？

lines.en: Which one? There are two within walking distance.
lines.zh: 哪个站？步行范围内有两个。

lines.en: The one near the museum — line 4, I think.
lines.zh: 博物馆旁边那个——应该是 4 号线。

lines.en: That's about a ten-minute walk, straight down this street, then left at the church.
lines.zh: 走过去大概十分钟，沿这条街一直走，到教堂左转。

lines.en: Straight, then left at the church. And is it signposted?
lines.zh: 一直走，教堂左转。那儿有路牌指示吗？

lines.en: Mostly. But the sign's small — look up, not at the shops.
lines.zh: 基本有。但牌子小——抬头看，别盯店铺。

lines.en: Got it. Could I take a bus instead, if I get lost?
lines.zh: 明白了。万一迷路，我能坐公交吗？

lines.en: Bus 11 stops right there. But walking's quicker at this hour.
lines.zh: 11 路公交就在那儿停。不过这会儿走路更快。

lines.en: Perfect, I'll walk. Thank you, you saved me.
lines.zh: 太好了，我走过去。谢谢你，帮了大忙。

lines.en: No problem — enjoy the museum.
lines.zh: 不客气——博物馆好好玩。

dialogs.title: Scheduling a Meeting by Email
dialogs.goal: 练习礼貌提议时间、协调多人日程、提前同步议程与跟进。

lines.en: Hi Mark, hoping to sync on the Q3 research plan — do you have 30 minutes next week?
lines.zh: Mark 你好，想就三季度研究计划对齐一下——下周你有 30 分钟吗？

lines.en: Wednesday looks open. Morning your time?
lines.zh: 周三好像有空。你那边上午？

lines.en: Wednesday 10am works. Should we include Lena from insights?
lines.zh: 周三上午十点可以。要把洞察部的 Lena 也拉上吗？

lines.en: Yes, she owns the consumer data. Send the invite and I'll add her.
lines.zh: 要，消费数据是她负责的。你发邀约，我来加她。

lines.en: Done. I'll share the agenda beforehand so we don't wander.
lines.zh: 发了。我会提前发议程，免得跑题。

lines.en: Please do — last time we spent 20 minutes on the wrong slide.
lines.zh: 务必——上次我们拿错幻灯片耗了 20 分钟。

lines.en: Noted. I'll keep it to three points: scope, timeline, owners.
lines.zh: 记下了。我控制三个点：范围、时间线、责任人。

lines.en: That's the Mark I like. Anything you need from me before?
lines.zh: 这才对味。会前你需要我做什么？

lines.en: Just your take on the budget ceiling. I don't want to over-promise.
lines.zh: 就你对预算上限的看法。我不想过度承诺。

lines.en: I'll send a one-liner by Tuesday. Talk Wednesday.
lines.zh: 周二前我发一句话给你。周三聊。
